extracted.intended_audience: Predoctoral fellowship applicants and their mentors/administrators (NIH NRSA F31 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling an NIH Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA Individual Predoctoral Fellowship (Parent F31) application, including required SF424/R&R forms, research plan, training plan, vertebrate animal justification, facilities/resources, and resource sharing statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA and application format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIAID posts sample applications; formats may change over time. Use the FOA-specific instructions (PA-16-309 for this sample) and current application forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) Cover Page completeness and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete SF 424 (R&R) cover page fields including type of submission, dates, applicant organization, authorized representative, and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing, the authorized representative certifies that statements are true and agrees to required assurances; include Federal Identifier, Agency Routing Number, and ensure signatures/dates are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project/Performance Site Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide project/performance site primary location(s), congressional district, and DUNS/EIN as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify primary organization (e.g., Vanderbilt University) and project congressional district (e.g., TN-005); include additional locations if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Other Project Information declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether human subjects, vertebrate animals, proprietary information, environmental impact, historic site status, and international activities are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, indicate exemption status, IRB pending/approval. If vertebrate animals are used, indicate IACUC pending/approval and provide Animal Welfare Assurance Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents with required attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed Table of Contents listing all application components and attachment filenames (e.g., Project Summary, Project Narrative, Bibliography, Facilities, Equipment, PHS Fellowship Supplemental).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure page numbering and filenames (e.g., M-4_Project_Summary.pdf) are accurate to facilitate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise summary describing the problem, central hypothesis, preliminary data, methods, specific aims, and potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include overarching objective, central hypothesis (e.g., MyD88 role in osteoclast differentiation), model systems to be used (murine osteomyelitis model), and implications for therapeutics and broad relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (Public Health Relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short statement describing the relevance of the project to public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the research will advance understanding or development of therapeutics (e.g., describe how bone remodeling is altered by infection and immune responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State clear, testable specific aims that follow from the central hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be feasible within the proposed period, distinct yet integrated, and tied to preliminary data and overall hypothesis (e.g., Aim 1: TLR/IL-1R signaling and osteoclast differentiation; Aim 2: MyD88 signaling in skeletal cells affects clearance and remodeling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy (Approach, Preliminary Data, Rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe experimental approach, preliminary data supporting feasibility, rationale for selected models/methods, and how data will test the hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include model advantages (e.g., genetically modified animals, high-resolution imaging), experimental assays (in vitro osteoclastogenesis, in vivo infection), expected outcomes, and how results will be interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Background and Goals for Fellowship Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain applicant's prior experience, training needs, and how the fellowship will support career development toward independent research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail mentor committee composition, coursework/training (e.g., VPMM, ASPIRE), presentation expectations, and planned milestones (seminars, journal clubs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Institutional Environment and Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional resources, intellectual environment, core facilities, seminars, and administrative support that will contribute to the trainee's success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention lab space, access to imaging and animal cores, BRET/ASPIRE programs, and examples of mentorship and collaboration; demonstrate how the institution enables completion of proposed aims and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources (laboratory, animal facility, cores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed descriptions of lab space, equipment, animal facilities (AAALAC accreditation), computer resources, and other institutional resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe biosafety level, dedicated culture spaces, specialized equipment (microscopes, imaging cores), shared computing resources and software (FIJI, GraphPad Prism), and animal care oversight structures (IACUC, DAC, OAWA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment listing
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment available to support the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both lab-specific and shared/core equipment (e.g., plate readers, gel imagers, microscopes) and indicate access arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals — Procedures and Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed description of animal procedures (species/strains, surgical methods, anesthesia, analgesia), justification for species, and relevance to the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe infection model procedures step-by-step (e.g., trephination, inoculation), anesthesia (isoflurane percentages), analgesia regimen (0.1 mg/kg buprenorphine pre-op and every 12 hours for 48 hours), monitoring frequency, and rationale for using mice and genetically modified strains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals — Number justification and statistical power
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit numbers of animals required per aim, sex inclusion plans, sample size calculations, expected effect size and power assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give per-aim animal counts (e.g., Specific Aim 1: 120 mice; Aim 2: 420 mice), justify group sizes (e.g., 10 mice per group to detect 50% difference with SD 35% and 80% power, two independent trials of 5 mice each), and explain breeding strategies for genetic models (Cre-Lox mating ratios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals — Veterinary care and animal welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe veterinary oversight, husbandry, monitoring, criteria for intervention/withdrawal, measures to limit pain/distress, and euthanasia methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State accreditation (AAALAC, USDA), daily monitoring routines, criteria for euthanasia (≥20% weight loss, signs of secondary wound infection), analgesia schedule, and euthanasia method (CO2 displacement rate 10–30% chamber volume per minute followed by cervical dislocation per AVMA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals — IACUC review and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether IACUC review is pending or approved and provide Animal Welfare Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IACUC approval is pending, state anticipated approval status and compliance with institutional policies; ensure all personnel complete required training modules (e.g., ABSL-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan — Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to timely distribution of data and methods (publication and deposit in PubMed Central) and presentation at scientific meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State intention to publish in peer-reviewed journals and deposit accepted manuscripts in NIH PubMed Central according to policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan — Model Organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to sharing newly generated model organisms with the research community under NIH model organism policies and standard MTAs/UBMTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide protocols and phenotypic data on request, avoid reach-through requirements, and ensure broad availability even if IP arises (consistent with NIH Principles and Guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the plan for training in the responsible conduct of research as part of the fellowship training requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List institutional RCR modules, attendance at annual RCR sessions, and how RCR training is integrated into the trainee's plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Sponsor and Sponsor/Co-Sponsor statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed sponsor and co-sponsor statements describing mentoring, resources, and respective contributions to the trainee's project and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mentor roles, frequency of interactions, mentorship plans, and letters confirming institutional commitment and access to resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters documenting collaborations, access to specialized expertise, and commitments to provide materials/assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use letters to confirm specific contributions (e.g., complementary expertise in fracture repair, hypoxia regulation, local drug delivery) and to document availability of core services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational and data management resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail computing resources, software, and data management practices that support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List desktop/lab computers, software (FIJI, GraphPad Prism, ReadCube), networked servers for data sharing, and lab data access policies to facilitate collaboration and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and permitted use of sample application
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the application is copyrighted and may be used only for nonprofit educational purposes provided the document remains unchanged and authors/organizations are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources for accessibility issues; do not repurpose sample text without appropriate credit and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance and accessibility note
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples have been reformatted to improve accessibility; contact information is provided for accessibility assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accessibility problems occur, contact the listed office (deaweb@niaid.nih.gov) to request assistance.
